transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-03
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Helix SRE), Tom Nguyen (Platform Eng), Alicia Moreno (Head of AI), Ben Carter (DevOps)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
- Walkthrough of Redwood Console request audit trail, error grouping and triage flows focusing on HelixFinance production incidents.
- Demoed request-level playback, distributed trace correlation, and example of KV cache miss debug.
- Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs; security docs to be shared; Redwood to run synthetic replay for cost/latency metrics.

Topics Covered:
- Request audit trails and deterministic playback
- Error analysis and grouping heuristics (stack vs message-based)
- Trace correlation across microservices and model backend hops
- KV cache fallback and cold-start symptom detection
- Security: KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs retention
- Pilot scope and success metrics (p99 latency, error-rate delta, cost per 1k tokens)

Action Items (captured in header too):
- Marcus to run replay and share results (CSV + charts)
- Lena to send security packet and onboarding checklist
- Helix to provide 48h trace sample and list of top 3 pain points

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Lena: ok everyone thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. Um just to set context, this is a focused workshop on request audit and failure triage, we wanna show how Console surfaces the full request trail and how you can jump from an error to the model invocation and back to the app traces.
[00:18] Priya: yep hi, hi thanks. we've been seeing intermittent 504s when we overlay traffic spikes with Kubernetes scaling, and sometimes the logs don't map cleanly to tokens so it's, it's been tricky.
[00:30] Marcus: right, so we're gonna demo two things - the request playback to replay the exact request and the trace joiner that stitches together "request-id" across services. also we'll show where KV cache misses show up in the token timeline.
[00:42] Tom: quick Q, when you say "request-id" is that propagated by you automatically or we need to pass our own header?
[00:50] Marcus: good q - Redwood will accept your X-Request-Id header and also tags it in the response. if none present we synthesize one, but for correlation it's best you pass your own. (minor audio glitch)
[01:05] Ben: are there any privacy concerns with storing full request bodies in the console, like PII?
[01:12] Lena: yes great point. by default hosted drops user payload after 30 days, private can be set to 0 retention, and there's field-level masking. we'll include the retention table in the security packet.
[01:28] Alicia: also we need KMS integration for key separation between teams — is HSM supported?
[01:35] Marcus: KMS/HSM is supported on Private deployments. on hosted we integrate with managed KMS per-tenant, and you can bring your own key in Dedicated/private routes. we'll add the HSM note to the doc.
[01:50] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[02:03] Marcus: jumping into demo, screen share coming up — ok showing the console, top nav, request-inspector tab. here's a failed request with status 504, you can see timeline left to right: client request, routing, model decode, token emission.
[02:20] Marcus: note here in the timeline, you can see a sudden spike in model latency which correlates to a KV cache miss — the token timeline shows a 200ms gap where the backend did seq-resync.
[02:35] Priya: wait we had thought KV was local, where's the cache stored?
[02:40] Marcus: it's sharded per-host in Dedicated; in hosted it's a managed distributed KV. there's a visible label on the request that indicates cache hit/miss, but sometimes the label is noisy — transcription sometimes says "K-V" as "kay vee" in logs.
[02:58] Tom: can we filter requests by trace id across services, like join to our internal opentelemetry traces?
[03:05] Marcus: yes you can add your OTEL trace id or the X-Request-Id and Console will surface any external trace links if you've configured the trace forwarder. we have a small adapter that matches by trace/span ids. it'll be in the integration guide.
[03:22] Lena: quick qualification - what are your SLOs you're targeting? p99, p95?
[03:28] Priya: p99 450ms for inference, p95 220, we expect spikes during market open, so the big thing is graceful degradation and clear fallbacks.
[03:39] Marcus: right, so we'll show automatic fallback policies — here you can set route policies to degrade to a smaller model variant or reduce batch size when queueing exceeds threshold. we also capture the fallback reason in the audit trail.
[03:55] Alicia: hmm could that change behavior subtly on outputs? like if we downgrade mid-call will you indicate that?
[04:03] Marcus: yes, the request metadata includes a model variant field and the playback shows both the original and the fallback output when applicable. you can diff them in the console.
[04:18] Ben: latency vs cost tradeoff question — Dedicated with bigger GPUs sounds ideal for p99, but cost spikes. what's the standard approach?
[04:29] Lena: teams often use Dedicated for critical routes and Hosted for lower tier. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization and you'll get an estimate of cost delta per-1k tokens. we'll produce a sample calc for your traffic.
[04:45] Priya: that calc we'd love, especially tied to our token distribution.
[04:49] Marcus: we'll run a replay using your sample traces and produce a delta table: p50/p95/p99 and cost/1k tokens for candidate model variants.
[05:02] (silence, typing)
[05:25] Marcus: ok switching to error-grouping — Console groups errors by stack signature by default but you can switch to message-first when stacks are noisy, like in polyglot apps. sometimes the same root cause appears across services with distinct stack traces. here's an example where a middleware timeout bubbled as a model decode failure downstream.
[05:45] Priya: that matches our Friday incident — we saw decode errors but the root cause was our LB healthcheck flapping. is there a way to tie LB events into the timeline?
[05:55] Marcus: yes you can ingest custom events and attach them to traces; we also accept structured events via the events API so they appear inline in the request timeline.
[06:08] Tom: when you ingest events does that affect retention or cost?
[06:12] Marcus: small ingestion cost, retention is configurable per-tenant, of course long-term retention incurs storage charges, we'll show a projection in the replay results.
[06:25] Priya: curious about the replay — does it mutate state or is it read-only? we can't replay into production.
[06:31] Marcus: replays are isolated to a sandbox runtime by default — they can be run against a shadow environment, we do provide a "no-side-effects" mode that strips write intents. For Helix we'll set the replay to sandbox.
[06:45] Alicia: can the playback reproduce the exact model tokenization differences? we've seen micro-diffs.
[06:50] Marcus: yes, Console records the tokenization snapshot (model version + tokenizer hash). you can compare token-level diffs. sometimes tokenizers are nondeterministic across minor versions so we tag that.
[07:05] [07:05] Speaker 5: there's a lag in the UI...
[07:10] Marcus: oh small UI hiccup — switching view. here's the distributed trace view, you can expand spans, click into the model span and see payload size, quantization mode, and kernel selection notes when available.
[07:26] Tom: kernel selection notes? like which CUDA kernel was used?
[07:30] Marcus: it depends on environment visibility. in Dedicated we expose the selected kernel and quant path; in hosted we provide a curated summary not the low-level kernel names due to abstraction.
[07:45] Priya: on security one more thing — audit logs. we need exportable immutable audit logs for compliance, does Redwood support immutable exports to our S3?
[07:54] Lena: yes, audit logs can be exported to your object store with lifecycle policies and can be set to append-only via our integration with cloud audits or SIEM. we'll include a sample policy in the docs pack.
[08:10] Marcus: now a quick deep-dive into a real trace you provided — pulling sample trace id: hf-20260831-77b... ok this one shows a cold start on the model host plus an autoscaler spike. you see the queue depth climb then a handful of 429s and then retries that produced latency jitter.
[08:30] Priya: that matches timestamps on our monitoring, the autoscaler had a delayed scale-up. can Redwood trace the time spent waiting in the scheduler separate from model decode?
[08:39] Marcus: yes we break out: scheduler queue time, kernel launch time, model decode, network hop. those are separate spans. if you integrate host metrics we'll overlay CPU/GPU utilization.
[08:54] Ben: do you surface backoffs/retries chain? like if our SDK retries over a short window will that show as nested attempts?
[09:01] Marcus: yes nested attempts appear with a parent request; we collapse noisy retries by default but you can expand the full attempt tree.
[09:12] (murmur)
[09:20] Lena: ok let's talk pilot success metrics: I propose we measure three KPIs over a two week pilot — p99 inference latency, error-rate change for the triaged signatures, and cost per 10k tokens. does that sound reasonable?
[09:32] Alicia: yes but include signal quality — we need to ensure request sampling is high enough to catch spikes.
[09:38] Marcus: we'll configure sampling to 100% for the pilot window on the selected routes.
[09:44] Priya: sampling added cost?
[09:46] Marcus: minimal for telemetry; main cost is storage if you keep long retention, but pilot will be 14 days and we'll provide rolled-up metrics.
[09:56] Tom: on instrumentation, do we need to change our SDK usage? we use a custom wrapper around the Redwood client.
[10:01] Marcus: only two things: forward your X-Request-Id and enable debug headers for enriched traces. if you use our official SDK it auto-instruments. for your wrapper we can share a snippet.
[10:12] Priya: can you show how error grouping would have treated our Friday signature?
[10:15] Marcus: sure — opening the incidents list, searching for "decode error" — here's a cluster. you can see similar messages grouped, but then multiple stacks due to polyglot services. switching to message-first groups them by the exception text and surfaces the shared root cause quicker.
[10:36] (short pause)
[10:55] Marcus: demoing request inspector playback now — I'm going to click "replay" and you can see the request payload, token timeline, and a side-by-side response diff between production and a smaller model variant.
[11:10] Priya: when you replay do you keep the exact header set? we rely on a signature header for auth.
[11:16] Marcus: by default we preserve headers marked as safe; sensitive headers are redacted. you can opt-in to preserve via a secure vault connector for the pilot. that will be documented.
[11:30] Tom: any gotchas with streaming responses and replay?
[11:33] Marcus: streaming is replayed as chunks; we also simulate network delays if you enable that mode. occasionally the ordering of chunk arrival can cause small diffs but they are surfaced.
[11:48] Alicia: ok on the security front, if we do Dedicated, can we get SOC2 + on-site audit coordination?
[11:56] Lena: yes enterprise customers get audit support and an assigned security engineer. We'll coordinate.
[12:05] (laughter)
[12:12] Marcus: quick note on the Optimize recommendations — the tool suggested a quantized 4-bit path for one of your heavy routes which lowered cost by ~35% in our sims but added small quality delta; we can tie that to an eval suite.
[12:27] Priya: we want that eval suite to include edge-case prompts from pricing engines.
[12:32] Marcus: absolutely, include your prompt set and we'll run regression checks.
[12:38] (crosstalk)
[12:50] Marcus: wrapping up, I'll start the synthetic replay using the sample traces you gave last week. planning to run it overnight and share a spreadsheet with latency/cost numbers and recommendations.
[13:03] Lena: and I'll email the security artifacts and the Private deployment checklist. we'll also set a pilot kickoff invite for week of Sep 13.
[13:12] Priya: thanks, one follow-up — in the replay results can you break out p99 for token generation versus overall request time? that's crucial for us.
[13:20] Marcus: yes we'll include token-gen p99 and decode p99.
[13:26] Ben: final question: competitor note — MajorCloudAI has a similar request playback but it's not as integrated with model variant fallback. curious how Redwood compares on multi-model routing?
[13:36] Marcus: good callout — Redwood's routing policy engine is policy-first and you can target model variants per route with circuit-breakers; we'll include a comparison sheet.
[13:48] (small break in audio)
[14:02] Lena: thanks everyone. Quick recap of next steps: Marcus run replay & share results, Lena share security + docs, Helix provide traces and confirm pilot timeline. We'll follow up in email with invites.
[14:20] Alicia: thanks, feels actionable.
[14:26] (meeting wraps, people saying thanks)
